title: Dan Hurley: College Basketball in 2026 Is 'Total Chaos'
description: With the men's basketball roster set, UConn will not turn to the transfer portal after a Colorado judge ruled players in the Class of 2022 may return to college for a fifth year.
fullText:
Dan Hurley isn't about to jump into the transferportal, now that the ruling of a Colorado judge has made six or seven dozen playerseligible to play – at least for now, unless another court overturns that decision – in the 2026-27 season.

He made that clear Friday in speaking with reportersafter a team scrimmage. He's got the 15 men he plans to do battle with in theupcoming season, a campaign loaded with one A-list competitor after anotheruntil the rigorous Big East season begins.

Simply, Hurley will not be pursuing any of the membersof the Class of 2022 who have been granted a fifth year of eligibility.

"Our team is on the floor," he saidwithout hesitation.

Dog Days 😤 pic.twitter.com/DTb16mSNBV

Fans already know some of them: Demary,Mullins, Ross, Ball, another Ross.

Then there are the freshmen: Landrew. County.

And the transfers: Hines,Khamenia, Machowski, Nash and Shaw, Amosoz, Giltay and Džafic.

This is the roster Hurley and his staff put togetherin the weeks after their lossin the championship game of the Men's NCAA Tournament. A team created after they said goodbyeto five seniors and to four players who decided to search for a different landingspot in the transfer portal.

Each new player seemingly was selected to fill arole – experienced players either envisioned by Hurley as a starter or anecessary depth piece, freshmen intended to develop into standout collegeplayers.

An old-school coach assembled his team in anold-school manner.

Hurley has been coaching long enough that he knowsthe way college sports used to be – before NIL, before agents, before sharedrevenue, before the transfer portal and the havoc all of that has brought.

On Friday, he passionately conveyed his feelingsabout teams that are continuing to tinker with their rosters in the wake oflast week's ruling in Colorado.

👀 https://t.co/TYQ1XBn2u4 pic.twitter.com/obvbNKKvUf

"The art of what we do has been cheapened alittle bit," he said in his Friday media availability, speaking about the coachingprofession. "You can put together better teams, teams that can compete andnot have to identify young talent, develop that talent."

"Now," Hurley continued, "you can screw up highschool recruiting, you can screw up portal recruiting and not have a very goodteam, and start plucking from a group of players in August and put together ateam."

The ramifications of that? A team assembled at the lastminute, denied the time over the summer to jell. Players who had beenworking hard to gain an advantage in the battle for a starting spot, for example, suddenly finding themselves with a new role.

"Now, let's unleash 80 players into the sport in thefirst week of August. We can't go on like this. And anyone that acts like it'sgreat, it's fine, it's good for college basketball, they've already taken thestance that this is what they've wanted, and now they're just defending theirposition. It's total chaos and it's not sustainable."

title: Souza is expected to stay with Tottenham this season, De Zerbi is backing him to be a game-changer
description: Tottenham Hotspur defender Joao Victor de Souza Menezes was attracting interest in the transfer market as he seeks more playing time.However, according to Eduardo Burgos, the 20-year-old is poised to ...
fullText:
Tottenham Hotspur defender Joao Victor de Souza Menezes was attracting interest in the transfer market as he seeks more playing time.

However, according to Eduardo Burgos, the 20-year-old is poised to remain at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium for the season.

Spurs received three offers for the youngster from FC Porto – two official bids and a loan offer. Benfica were also reportedly interested.

It appears that Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi is backing him to be a game-changer for the North London club.

Souza joined from Brazil in January but struggled for game time with Destiny Udogie and Djed Spence ahead of him in the pecking order.

It was also a perilous time to throw in the youngster as the club battled to stave off relegation.

This summer would have been perfect for him to leave for European experience as Tottenham signed Andy Robertson, further bolstering the full-back position.

For all his potential, keeping Souza around for another season could do more harm than good to his development.

Lauded as 'forward-thinking and technically very good' by former Spurs manager Thomas Frank, Souza has a bright future.

But the teenager needs regular competitive football, not another year spent watching Udogie, Spence and now Robertson battle for minutes ahead of him.

That is why Tottenham should reconsider their stance and allow him to go to Portugal on loan.

The Portuguese giants have already shown serious interest, making them an ideal destination for Souza to test himself at a higher level while playing regularly.

There is little value in keeping a prospect at the club if De Zerbi cannot guarantee him meaningful minutes.

A season in Portugal could give Souza the experience, confidence and tactical education he needs before returning to North London ready to compete for a first-team place.

Spurs should let him go, earn his stripes and come back stronger.

title: Jose Mourinho ‘not angry’ after missing out on top midfield target, has full confidence on current squad
description: Real Madrid are now out of the race for Rodri, and it seems set that the club will not make any new midfield signings this summer beyond Bernardo Silva.There were rumours that Jose Mourinho was push...
fullText:
Real Madrid are now out of the race for Rodri, and it seems set that the club will not make any new midfield signings this summer beyond Bernardo Silva.

There were rumours that Jose Mourinho was pushing for a new defensive midfield signing, and Los Blancos saw the Manchester City star as the ideal candidate.

Rodri, however, preferred to join Barcelona and is very close to completing the move to Catalonia as matters stand. Moreover, he is said to have personally informed the Real Madrid administration of his decision out of respect.

Earlier this week, multiple reports suggested that Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho was infuriated by the club missing out on his top midfield target, especially given how the midfield has been Real Madrid's biggest weakness in recent times.

Rodri would have been the perfect midfield addition. (Photo by Annabel Lee-Ellis/Getty Images)

Ben Fernandes Santos, however, reveals that the real situation is far from the tension being suggested. In fact, Mourinho is reportedly not angry about how the Rodri saga unfolded.

There is no doubt that the coach would have gladly taken the Manchester City star in his plans, but it could not be done and the matter is closed. He is not angry on the board.

The journalist further adds that Mourinho currently has total confidence in the existing players and that he is ready to use the stars he currently has at his disposal.

Mourinho fully believes in his squad. (Photo by Christian Bruna/Getty Images)

He will test several of the recently returned players in the preseason friendly against Ferencvaros tomorrow, and hopes to get a feel of the profiles he has at his disposal.

In any case, Mourinho is genuinely excited about what's ahead and knows he can achieve great things with the current Real Madrid cohort. He believes he has the team to win him the biggest titles.

In recent hours, there have been suggestions that the coach plans to use Bernardo Silva in the double pivot after the Rodri operation fell apart, and there is a good chance the Portuguese star will be tested in that role in the coming days.

Should Silva work out alongside Aurelien Tchouameni, Real Madrid will have solved their biggest problem on the field.

title: Liverpool agree surprise deal to sign Barcelona captain on loan – Romano
description: Liverpool have pulled off one of the biggest surprises of the summer transfer window after reaching an agreement with Barcelona to sign Ronald Araujo on loan.It has come as quite a surprise, with the ...
fullText:
Liverpool have pulled off one of the biggest surprises of the summer transfer window after reaching an agreement with Barcelona to sign Ronald Araujo on loan.

It has come as quite a surprise, with the deal happening without much noise surrounding it, but the Uruguayan is set to play at Anfield this upcoming season.

According to Fabrizio Romano, the deal is now in its final stages, with all major terms agreed and documents expected to be signed within the next 24 hours.

Ronald Araujo is set for a new adventure in the Premier League. (Photo by Lars Baron/Getty Images)

Romano has revealed that Liverpool and Barcelona have reached a verbal agreement for Araujo's transfer, with sporting director Deco giving the green light to the operation.

The Uruguayan defender will join the Premier League champions on an initial loan, with the agreement including a buy option that Liverpool can choose whether to activate.

Importantly, the clause is not mandatory, meaning Barcelona retain some control over the defender's long-term future if Liverpool decide against making the move permanent.

Araujo's future at Barça has been the subject of constant speculation for quite some time now.

Having fallen down the pecking order in Hansi Flick's plans, Araujo looked determined to win his place back in Flick's team, but it looks like he has eventually chosen the option where he gets more game time.

Once regarded as one of Barcelona's untouchable players, injuries and growing competition at centre-back have complicated his standing in Hansi Flick's squad.

Araujo has also had forgettable moments on the biggest stage for Barça, thereby making it very difficult for the club to trust him going forward.

Araujo to become a Liverpool player. (Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty Images)

For Liverpool, this represents a significant defensive addition without committing to a permanent transfer immediately.

The buy option allows the Reds to assess Araujo over the course of the season before deciding whether to make the move permanent next summer.

If the 27-year-old rediscovers the form that once made him one of Europe's most highly rated defenders, Liverpool could secure a bargain. If not, they retain the flexibility to walk away.

From Barcelona's perspective, the move reduces their wage bill while keeping open the possibility of generating a sizeable transfer fee next summer.

Araujo now has a glorious opportunity to break away from the toxicity that surrounded him at Barça and play alongside a champion defender like Virgil van Dijk.

The Uruguayan could use this loan spell to return to his best level and enhance his reputation, and it remains to be seen how he progresses at Anfield.

title: Ziaire Williams: Playing for the Lakers is 'super surreal'
description: New Lakers forward and Southland native Ziaire Williams is thrilled to be playing for the Purple and Gold.
fullText:
One newcomer to the Los Angeles Lakers who hasn't been talked about as much as some of the others is Ziaire Williams. The 6-foot-9 forward is very athletic, reportedly has a vertical leap of nearly 40 inches, runs the floor well and finishes strong in transition and is a versatile, effective defender. He will have a chance to make a significant impact on a Lakers team that has badly needed versatile, athletic perimeter defenders for the last few years.

Williams was born in Lancaster, Calif., which is about an hour northeast of downtown Los Angeles, and he went to high school in the San Fernando Valley, first at Notre Dame High School and then at Sierra Canyon School. He's now back in the Southland, and in a video on the Lakers' YouTube channel, he said that getting to play for the team is "super surreal."

"Seeing my name on the Lakers jersey was super surreal, a blessing," Williams said. "I can't even explain it into words I'm just so excited to be back home, playing in front of the fans, my family and I never would've imagined this day would come true. Eight-year old me is doing backflips right now. It's crazy, I just can't wait to play a real game. I'm ready to play right now."

The 24-year-old's main weakness is his 3-point shooting, which has improved somewhat during his five years in the NBA, but he was at a mediocre 34.3% from that distance last season. He's very good at hitting wide-open 3s (defined as the closest defender being at least six feet away), but he tends to struggle when a defender is closer than six feet away from him.

Last season, Williams averaged 10.2 points, 2.4 rebounds, 1.1 assists, 1.4 steals and 0.4 blocks in 22.9 minutes a game as a member of the Brooklyn Nets. He signed a one-year, $2.45 million veteran minimum contract with the Lakers in mid-July.

fullText:
Tottenham Hotspur continues their pre-season preparations in a friendly encounter against the Spanish side Getafe on Saturday at the Spurs Training Centre.

Venue: Hotspur Way Training Centre, London.

Tottenham Hotspur manager Roberto De Zerbi faces a heavily disrupted squad ahead of today's friendly at Hotspur Way due to lingering injuries and post-World Cup workloads.

Midfielder James Maddison is completely sidelined after a recurrence of an old hip injury, leaving him in a race against time for the upcoming Premier League opener.

While Dejan Kulusevski and Mohammed Kudus are progressing well from long-term knee and quadriceps issues, this fixture comes too soon for their match involvement.

On a positive note, Mateus Fernandes is expected to return to action against Getafe after resting for calf fatigue. Long-term absentees Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert remain ruled out with severe cruciate ligament injuries.

However, the squad receives a major boost as World Cup participants Rodrigo Bentancur and Pape Matar Sarr, alongside new signing Marcos Senesi, have rejoined training and are fully available for selection.

Getafe CF manager José Bordalás has been forced to adapt his tactical plans following a devastating, late pre-season blow to his midfield.

Christantus Uche suffered a catastrophic right-knee injury involving multiple ligament and meniscus tears from a reckless tackle against Monaco, ruling him out for the entire upcoming season as he awaits major surgery.

Despite this massive setback, Getafe's squad is bolstered by several fully fit summer additions.

New signings Ramón Terrats, Saba Sazonov, and Zaid Romero are all expected to receive minutes today to build on-field cohesion before their domestic campaign kicks off.

Additionally, forward Martin Satriano enters this fixture in excellent physical condition and rich goalscoring form, having netted two pre-season goals already, and he is fully prepared to lead the Spanish side's attack in this closed-doors encounter.

The Lilywhites kicked off their preparations with consecutive shutouts, defeating Milton Keynes Dons 1–0 and Auckland FC 2–0. They followed that up with a 1–1 draw against Sydney FC, which they won 4–2 on penalties. Most recently, Spurs secured a high-profile 2–1 victory over Chelsea in Sydney, showcasing great resilience after a late winner from striker Richarlison.

Getafe CF has experienced highly mixed results and form during their summer preparations under José Bordalás. The Spanish side opened their pre-season positively, securing a 1–0 win over Reading and a 2–1 victory against Tenerife. However, their momentum has completely stalled in recent weeks. title: Aaron McKenna vs. Etinosa Oliha live results, round-by-round updates, ring walks, start time for Zuffa Boxing 10
description: Follow Aaron McKenna vs. Etinosa Oliha and Callum Walsh vs. Tyler Denny live results and round-by-round updates for the Zuffa Boxing 10 fight card on Saturday in Dublin, Ireland.
fullText:
Uncrowned has Aaron McKenna vs. Etinosa Oliha and Callum Walsh vs. Tyler Denny live results, round-by-round updates, highlights, ring walks and start time for the Zuffa Boxing 10 fight card on Saturday at the 3Arena in Dublin, Ireland. Aaron McKenna and Etinosa Oliha clash for the vacant IBF middleweight title in the main event, while rising star Callum Walsh takes on the former European champion Tyler Denny to complete the middleweight doubleheader.

Ireland's McKenna (20-0, 10 KOs) was last in action when he dominated Liam Smith for a wide unanimous decision win in April 2025.

Oliha (22-0, 10 KOs) defeated Alexander Pavlov in an IBF eliminator in late 2024. He has fought just once since, getting a third-round TKO win over Ivan Njegac last September.

Walsh (16-0, 11 KOs) moved up to middleweight in his last fight and survived a knockdown to take a decision over Carlos Ocampo in January.

title: 'Having skill is one thing': Shikhar Dhawan drops big verdict on Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
description: Former India opener Shikhar Dhawan has praised teenage batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, saying the youngster's fearless batting and ability to perform at such a young age make him special.  Speaking to news agency ANI, Dhawan said it is a big achievement for a 15-year-old to reach the international level and deliver consistent performances.  Dhawan said talent alone is not enough, and added that having the courage and mindset to play attacking cricket at such a young age is what sets Sooryavanshi apart.
fullText:
Former India opener Shikhar Dhawan has praised teenage batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, saying the youngster's fearless batting and ability to perform at such a young age make him special.

Speaking to news agency ANI, Dhawan said it is a big achievement for a 15-year-old to reach the international level and deliver consistent performances. He also pointed to Sooryavanshi's IPL displays, saying the teenager's confidence in hitting boundaries stands out.

Dhawan said talent alone is not enough, and added that having the courage and mindset to play attacking cricket at such a young age is what sets Sooryavanshi apart. He also backed the youngster to continue doing well in the years ahead.

"He is batting very superbly. And it's a very big thing that at the age of 15 or 16, reaching the international level first is a big thing in itself. Even when he was playing in the IPL. But the way he hits fours and sixes, that's a wonderful thing. Having skill is one thing, but having the heart for it, and that too at 15, is a very big thing. And I'm sure that his present is also very good and his future will also be very good," Dhawan said.

Sooryavanshi, 15, recently enjoyed a successful T20I series against Zimbabwe, scoring 151 runs in three matches to win his maiden Player of the Series award as India completed a 3-0 clean sweep.

Earlier, during the T20I series against England, Sooryavanshi became the youngest player to make his international debut for India.

His India debut came after a successful IPL 2026 season with Rajasthan Royals. He scored 776 runs at a strike rate of 237.30, including one century and five fifties. He finished as the tournament's highest run-scorer and hit a record 72 sixes.

Sooryavanshi also won the Orange Cap, Most Valuable Player, Emerging Player, Super Striker and Super Sixes awards after the season.

Earlier this year, he also impressed in the ICC Men's Under-19 Cricket World Cup, scoring 439 runs and winning the Player of the Tournament award.

fullText:

With the 2026 FIFA World Cup over and club teams now returning to preseason action, the excitement is building for the start of competitive club action for the 2026/27 season.

As the most visible and profitable league in the world, many eyes around the globe are fixated on when the Premier League will get going again.

Defending champions Arsenal will look to win their first-ever back-to-back Premier League titles, while Manchester City, Chelsea, and Liverpool — all under new management — are expected to challenge for the prize.

title: Chelsea vs AC Milan – Match preview and team news
description: Chelsea travels to Indonesia for another pre-season friendly as they face AC Milan on Saturday at the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium.Chelsea vs AC Milan – Match preview and team newsDate: Saturday, 8th ...
fullText:
Chelsea travels to Indonesia for another pre-season friendly as they face AC Milan on Saturday at the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium.

Venue: Gelora Bung Karno Stadium, Jakarta, Indonesia.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso faces significant selection dilemmas ahead of the friendly in Jakarta, primarily driven by a heavily depleted squad following the World Cup. A large contingent of first-team regulars—including Enzo Fernández, Reece James, Malo Gusto, Jordan Henderson, Maxence Lacroix, Morgan Rogers, and Valentín Barco—remain entirely unavailable as they build up fitness. On a positive note, Cole Palmer and Levi Colwill are expected to return to action after being rested against Juventus due to minor knocks. Mykhailo Mudryk is also in line for increased minutes, building on his brief substitute appearance which marked his return to football after a 20-month anti-doping suspension. Meanwhile, Trevoh Chalobah has been left out of the touring squad entirely as he edges closer to a permanent transfer away from Stamford Bridge. This leaves room for new signings like Danny Welbeck and young winger Geovany Quenda to push for starting roles.

AC Milan manager Rúben Amorim is dealing with notable high-profile absences for this pre-season fixture. Former Chelsea winger Christian Pulisic is officially ruled out, denying him a reunion with his old club due to a persistent thigh injury picked up during his World Cup campaign. Milan will also be without newly signed defender Mario Gila, who is currently sidelined with an injury and will play no part in the match. Despite these setbacks, Christopher Nkunku is fully available and expected to feature prominently after scoring the equalizer against rivals Inter Milan in their previous outing. With a very short turnaround following the intense Milan derby played in Perth, Amorim is heavily tipped to rotate his starting eleven. This tactical shuffle is expected to hand starts to veteran midfielder Luka Modrić and forward Gonçalo Ramos as the Italian side looks to manage player workloads.

Chelsea's pre-season form is currently stuttering under new manager Xabi Alonso. After kicking off their preparations with a win against Western Sydney Wanderers, the Blues have hit a rough patch. They suffered consecutive losses in their most recent outings, losing a tight encounter to Tottenham Hotspur before falling 1-0 to Juventus in Hong Kong.

AC Milan has displayed resilient but mixed form during their summer tour under Rúben Amorim. The Italian side has played out successive draws against heavy competition. They opened with a high-scoring 2-2 draw against Scottish champions Celtic and followed it up with a hard-fought 1-1 draw against city rivals Inter Milan in Perth, courtesy of a Christopher Nkunku equalizer.

title: Aaron Donald Responds to Rams Return Buzz After Practice Appearance
description: Los Angeles Rams star Aaron Donald is getting closer to coming back, and on Friday, August, he finally spoke about his possible return. The post Aaron Donald Responds to Rams Return Buzz After Practice Appearance appeared first on LA Sports Report.
fullText:
Day by day, Los Angeles Rams star Aaron Donald is getting closer to coming back, and on Friday, August, he finally spoke about his possible return.

Donald has put his head down and focused on his workouts over the past few weeks as he tests himself to see what he can handle.

While the Rams were practicing at Loyola Marymount on Friday, the edge rusher had a workout at UCLA, eventually getting the attention of some fans, and one of them asked if he was coming back to the Rams.

"I don't know yet. We're going to see," the LA legend said.

Donald is only 35 years old, and he retired at 33, looking to go out on top while still playing at a high level.

No doubt, all of the double and triple teams that he faced were starting to wear on him, along with no real goal for him to aim at.

He already delivered LA a Super Bowl, became recognized as the best non-quarterback player in the NFL for years on end, and THE defender of his generation as well.

Donald racked up endless All-Pros and Defensive Player of the Year awards, and when he walked away, there was nothing left.

However, things changed when the Rams traded for Myles Garrett, and all of a sudden, he gets the chance to share the field with a defender just as special as him.

Donald had a workout with the Rams, using their equipment. He did individual drills with Rams defensive line coach Giff Smith, trainer Reggie Scott and strength coach Justin Lovett.

Donald speaks nearly every day with head coach Sean McVay, according to the coach, with an open line of communication.

"He's got such an intentional routine and rhythm. He's taking great care of himself, as we all know," McVay said.

"Getting ready to play football and just working out the way that he has, there's a little bit of a different rhythm and routine."

The Rams and Donald agreed not to decide anything until the team returns to Woodland Hills.

Their first practice at the facility is on Saturday, when McVay will again face questions. At this point, for Rams fans, there is enough smoke to get really excited about Donald returning to wreak havoc in the pocket.

title: FIFA president Gianni Infantino faces fresh scrutiny over alleged UEFA affair and six-figure pay-off
description: Gianni Infantino’s time at UEFA is under scrutiny after new allegations that the football body paid a six-figure settlement to a former employee who was involved in a relationship with the now FIFA ...
fullText:
Gianni Infantino's time at UEFA is under scrutiny after new allegations that the football body paid a six-figure settlement to a former employee who was involved in a relationship with the now FIFA president.

According to an investigation by The Telegraph, the woman was allegedly promoted while the relationship was ongoing before leaving UEFA with a substantial payment.

The report claims UEFA also funded an MBA for the former employee at a business school, with annual fees said to have been around £45,000.

UEFA has confirmed that a payment was made, along with funding for the MBA, although they insist both were permitted under the regulations governing staff departures at the time.

The organisation said those rules have since been tightened, with its current regulations designed to reflect the standards expected of a modern, high-profile organisation.

Infantino, who joined UEFA in 2000 before becoming its general secretary and eventually taking over as FIFA president in 2016, strongly denies the allegations.

A FIFA spokesperson said there had never been a complaint from an employee concerning Infantino's behaviour.

They described any suggestion of inappropriate conduct or regulatory breaches as categorically untrue.

The Telegraph's report claims the alleged then-UEFA president Michel Platini knew of the relationship and confronted Infantino, demanding that either he or the woman leave.

Sources cited by the publication claim the woman subsequently left UEFA with a pay-off and later secured another position in the football industry.

The allegations come at a very difficult time for Infantino, whose leadership of FIFA has faced criticism following the collapse of a controversial financing proposal involving outside investors.

UEFA recently voted unanimously to oppose the plan, while concerns over FIFA's commercial direction have continued to grow.

Still, Infantino remains determined to continue in his role and has reportedly told those close to him that he has no intention of stepping down.

The latest allegations will likely add more pressure on a FIFA president already facing a vocal backlash from within the beautiful game.

title: European Athletics Championships: what you need to know
description: Birmingham's Alexander Stadium will welcome competitors from about 50 countries for seven days.
fullText:
More than 1,500 of Europe's best athletes are set to descend on Birmingham this month as the city hosts the European Athletics Championships.

The renovated Alexander Stadium will welcome competitors from about 50 countries for seven days.

Organisers have promised "elite performances, homegrown heroes and edge-of-your-seat finals".

Here is everything you need to know.

The championships will take place at Alexander Stadium in Perry Barr, Birmingham.

First opened in 1976, the stadium became the home of UK Athletics in 2011 before undergoing a redevelopment ahead of the 2022 Commonwealth Games.

It is said to be the largest athletics stadium in the UK, seating around 18,000 people.

The North Stand has been renamed the Matthew Hudson-Smith Stand in honour of the Wolverhampton-born Olympic medallist and four-time European champion.

Spectators have been advised not to drive to the venue as Alexander Stadium will operate as a car-free venue for the event.

There will be no spectator parking available at the stadium or in the surrounding local area.

A pre-booked shuttle bus will run from Birmingham city centre. The pick-up point is James Watt Queensway.

For those travelling by train, Perry Barr railway station is the nearest stop, about a 20-minute walk from the stadium.

Perry Barr is regularly serviced by trains running from Birmingham New Street Station, Rugeley, Walsall, and Wolverhampton with additional services running on event days.

Bus services including the 51, X51 and 52 stop near Perry Avenue, while the 33, 907, 907A, 934, 935, 936, 937, 937A and 997 stop close to Perry Park.

Birmingham Airport is also expected to welcome athletes and spectators from across Europe.

The championships run from Monday until 16 August with competition taking place across seven days.

The action begins on Monday with the men's hammer and women's shot put events, plus sprint and hurdles on the track, with the first medals handed out including the winner of the men's 5000m final.

The final day features nine finals, including 4x400m relays, the 4x100m relay, the women's 1500m and the men's pole vault.

There will also be "one-day deciders" where events like the 100m sprint will go from heats through to the final on the same day.

A host of Olympic and world champions are expected to compete.

Great Britain's 98-strong team includes Olympic 800m champion Keely Hodgkinson, sprinter Dina Asher-Smith and heptathlete Katarina Johnson-Thompson.

As well as 400m star Hudson-Smith, who was born in Wolverhampton, there are several athletes from the West Midlands in Team GB, including middle-distance runner Issy Boffey and marathon runner Ellis Cross from Birmingham.

High jumper Joel Clarke-Khan and marathon runner Rose Harvey both hail from Worcestershire, while Clara Evans, another marathon runner, is from Hereford. Relay runners Josh Faulds and Jake Minshull are from Rugby and Coventry respectively, and long jumper Jazmin Sawyers is from Stoke-on-Trent.

From elsewhere in the world, Swedish pole vault world record holder Mondo Duplantis, Dutch star Femke Bol, Italy's Nadia Battocletti and Mattia Furlani, Portugal's Isaac Nader and Norway's Jakob Ingebrigtsen are all expected to feature.

Britain heads into the championships as the most successful nation in the event's history, having won 134 medals, including 50 golds.

The championships will be shown live across the BBC.

Coverage begins on BBC Two at 10:30 BST on Monday, with action throughout the week on BBC One, BBC Two and iPlayer.

BBC Radio 5 Live and BBC Sounds will provide daily live commentary, while the BBC Sport website and app will feature live coverage, reports, analysis and video clips.

Jeanette Kwakye will present the morning television coverage, with Gabby Logan hosting in the evenings. They will be joined by Olympic medallists and athletics experts including Jessica Ennis-Hill, Greg Rutherford and Jenny Meadows.

Follow BBC Birmingham on BBC Sounds, Facebook, X and Instagram.

title: Coventry City fan keeping it Sky Blue in Dorset
description: How John Lovegrove ended up living on Highfield Road and Coventry Close on the south coast.
fullText:
A Coventry City fan who moved more than 100 miles away from his beloved team ended up in Dorset living on Highfield Road before relocating to Coventry Close.

"I can't get rid of the Coventry connection," said Sky Blues-mad John Lovegrove.

Highfield Road was the name of City's original home ground, and his address there on the south coast had been pure coincidence, he said. But he addmitted to being more conscious of what he was doing when choosing his Coventry Close abode.

The supporter has lived in Dorset since 1998, making a round trip of more than 300 miles for every Sky Blues home game.

"There's actually a lot of Coventry fans down here, mainly in Bournemouth," the 76-year-old said. "But as far as I'm aware, I'm the only Sky Blues fan on Coventry Close."

Lovegrove went to his first Coventry game when he was nine, when Jimmy Hill was the manager and said his favourite player then was George Hudson, whom he said "made it look so easy".

Lovegrove had a season ticket for more than 20 years when he lived in Coventry and has one again - despite living 156 miles away - for the club's new Premier League campaign.

"I car-share with my son and two others who live down here. We met them by accident at an away match in Plymouth. We sat next to them, got talking, found out we all had season tickets and started car-sharing. That was three years ago."

Assuming he went to every game at the Coventry Building Society Arena in the last three years, Lovegrove has clocked up at least 20,700 miles doing the round trip.

As for his other fan credentials, he said he had seen every game City had played at Wembley bar one.

"I was there in 1987 for the FA Cup final, the Charity Shield the following year, the Checkatrade Trophy (2017), the Division 2 play-off final (2018) and the FA Cup semi-final against Manchester United.

"The only one I missed was the Championship promotion play-off against Luton, because I couldn't get a ticket."

However, despite his passion for the Sky Blues, he might not be able to make Coventry City's first game in the Premier League for 25 years, when they face Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium on 21 August.

"I'm hoping to get to Arsenal, but I'm in the ballot for that. But my son Scott, he will be there."

title: U.S. Women's Amateur weathers third suspension in 3 days
description: Severe weather suspended Round of 16 play at the 2026 U.S.
fullText:
OLTEWAH, Tenn. — For the third straight day, Mother Nature showed no mercy at the U.S. Women's Amateur.

Just as was the case on Wednesday and Thursday here at the Honors Course, wild weather conditions halted play Friday afternoon with all eight Round of 16 matches underway. Unlike the first two days, though, on Friday play never resumed.

After nearly three hours of rain and repeated lightning flashes, the USGA suspended the matches for the remainder of the day, citing unsafe conditions. Play is expected to resume Saturday at 7 a.m. ET.

As the course was assessed for potential damage, a tree behind the 18th green was discovered to have been struck by lightning. The tree sustained a long vertical gash, while bark and pieces of wood were scattered throughout the surrounding area. One piece of debris was even driven into the side of a nearby practice green. It remains unclear whether the storm caused any additional damage to the course.

Among the most intriguing story lines is 14-year-old Maggie Jiayi Ma of Irvine, Calif., who is the youngest player in the 156-player field and making a run at becoming the youngest champion in Women's Amateur history. In her Round of 16 match against U.S. Girls' Junior champion Clairey Lin, Ma is tied through four holes.

title: Try not to cry watching Phillies legend Chase Utley’s Wall of Fame speech
description: Chase Utley delivered a Wall of Fame speech that captured exactly why he became one of Philadelphia's most beloved athletes ever.
fullText:
Try not to cry watching Phillies legend Chase Utley's Wall of Fame speech appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

Chase Utley put the finishing touch on his Phillies legacy Friday night, and he did it with a speech that captured exactly what made him a franchise icon. The former second baseman was inducted into the Phillies Wall of Fame before the team's game against the Toronto Blue Jays at Citizens Bank Park, becoming the 51st inductee in franchise history.

Utley delivered an emotional address that reflected on what the city and organization meant to him over his 13 seasons in Philadelphia.

"You don't really just play in Philly. You survive it, you earn it, and if you're lucky, you grow from it," Utley said. "To me, this city is about passion, it's about emotion, it's about toughness, but most of all, it's about winning."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Earned, not given 🤝 pic.twitter.com/cKSlQLhDYX

— NBC Sports Philadelphia (@NBCSPhilly) August 8, 2026

Utley spoke to the standard the city held him to throughout his career, one he said pushed him to become the player he ultimately became.

"For 13 years, I tried to play the game that this city expects us to play. Hard, honest, no shortcuts, no excuses, and you let me know every night whether I was doing my job," Utley said. "That's what I love most about this city. Because in Philadelphia, you don't get respect, you have to earn respect. And standing here tonight, knowing I may have earned a small piece of that respect from you, that means more to me than everything."

He closed by expressing gratitude for everything the city gave him in return.

"Philly, you gave me so much. You gave me a career, you gave me teammates who would eventually become family, you gave me a championship," Utley said. "And now, to have my name forever connected to this organization and this city, that's something I will carry with myself forever. So thank you, Philadelphia, for everything you gave me, and for making me feel like a part of your family. I will always be proud to be a Philadelphia Philly."

The induction capped a career that made Utley one of the most beloved players in franchise history.

A first-round pick in 2000, Utley helped lead the Phillies through the greatest sustained run in franchise history, five straight NL East titles from 2007 to 2011, two pennants, and the 2008 World Series championship.

Across 1,551 games in Philadelphia, he hit .282/.366/.481 with 259 home runs, 1,025 RBIs, and 1,103 runs scored, and he remains tied for the World Series record with five home runs in a single Fall Classic from the 2009 series. He is now considered a strong Hall of Fame candidate, drawing 65.5 percent support on this year's early BBWAA ballot tracking.

Utley became the third member of the 2008 championship team to join the Wall of Fame, following Jimmy Rollins and former general manager Ed Wade, whose inductions came a year earlier.

title: Liverpool agree surprise deal to sign Barcelona defender Ronald Araujo
description: Liverpool have agreed a loan deal for Barcelona defender Ronald Araujo, according to Fabrizio Romano.The Reds desperately needed a new centre-half as they are dangerously short-manned at the back foll...
fullText:
Liverpool have agreed a loan deal for Barcelona defender Ronald Araujo, according to Fabrizio Romano.

The Reds desperately needed a new centre-half as they are dangerously short-manned at the back following the departure of Ibrahima Konate.

Liverpool signed Giovanni Leoni last summer, but he picked up a long-term injury before he could even find his footing. He is still getting up to speed.

The Merseyside outfit purchased Jeremy Jacquet in January, but soon after, he also picked up an injury that sidelined him for months.

Joe Gomez has suffered an injury in pre-season, too, leaving Liverpool light in the rearguard ahead of the resumption of the Premier League.

They have now responded by signing the Barca captain. Injuries have derailed his trajectory over the past few seasons, but on his day, he is still a formidable unit.

The 27-year-old featured 24 times in La Liga (only 11 starts) last season. He still managed three goals and helped to keep two clean sheets,

Araujo won 67 percent of his aerial and 57% of his ground duels. If he can stay fit, he is quite the pick-up for Andoni Iraola's side.

However, Liverpool will be holding their breath that Araujo can finally put his fitness problems behind him.

The Uruguayan international (27 caps) has endured a frustrating couple of seasons, with injuries interrupting his rhythm and limiting his availability.

That makes this loan a gamble for the Reds.

There is little doubt about Araujo's ability when he is fit. His physicality, aggression and experience could make a huge difference.

Former Barca boss Luis Enrique lauded him as a 'top player', but the biggest question is whether he can stay on the pitch.

Araujo has started just 22 league games across the past two seasons, underlining just how unavailable he has been.

If he breaks down again, Liverpool could quickly find themselves back at square one.

title: Did Hampshire club shape Brazil's football magic?
description: Radio Solent's Tom Murray explores the link between Southampton and the father of football in Brazil.
fullText:
The connection between Brazil and football is legendary. It is one defined by flair, passion and five FIFA World Cup titles.

Not to mention Pele, Ronaldo and, for Southampton and Bournemouth fans, there are Leo Cienza, Evan Ilsen and Haiyan.

Just how did the South American country, home to the world's largest carnival, become so good at the beautiful game? The answer may be much closer to home in Hampshire.

Radio Solent's Tom Murray headed to St Mary's Stadium in Southampton to find out more.

Either side of a railway footbridge, just before the ground itself, is a mural depicting famous players of Southampton's past, including Alan Shearer, Matt Le Tissier and Ricky Lambert.

But look closer and in the middle of a red-painted "1885" - the year Southampton Football Club was founded - is a black and white image of a man, sporting a terrific moustache.

It is a depiction of Charles Miller, considered to be the father of football in Brazil.

"It's quite an amazing story," said Andy Skinner, who has worked at Southampton museums for more than a decade.

"He was born in Sao Paulo to British parents and, like lots of expats at that time, they decided to send the young Charles back to England to be educated," he explained.

Charles returned by ship to Southampton, where he attended a boarding school.

"Clearly his education that he gets here is pretty sports heavy," said Skinner.

"He's introduced to football and, when he's in Southampton, he plays for St Mary's, which becomes Southampton, and there's another team as well called Corinthians."

The young man was "really impressed" not only with the game itself but "the way in which these teams that he's encountering play it", he said.

Miller spent about 10 years in Southampton before taking the step that would shape Brazilian football forever, according to Duncan Holley, historian at Southampton FC.

Aged 19, Miller returned to the country he was born in, armed with "some footballs, a rule book, some Saints shirts and sort of officially introduced football to Brazil", said Holley.

"The fact that he had the rule book was pretty handy, I should think, because not many people in Brazil would have known the rules of association football as they were then.

"He came from a well-to-do family, so that obviously helped, but he lived in Sao Paulo and he didn't waste much time in setting up teams, getting up, going around the streets, getting boys together, men together, to form teams and then leagues."

In 1904, 10 years after Miller's return, Southampton toured Argentina - the first English side to do so, said Holley.

"He went all the way down to meet the boat as it docked in Rio on their way to Argentina," he said.

"He obviously saw their arrival as a way of promoting in Brazil the game of football and, in fact, he tried to get them to come and play a game in Brazil but they were already committed to Argentina so he had to wait another 44 years before Southampton toured Brazil in 1948."

Miller's legacy lives on in Sao Paolo's football museum, in the city's Charles Miller Square, where the history, culture and legends of Brazilian football are celebrated.

Marcel Tonini, a researcher at the museum, said he believes while there may have been others who also introduced the game to Brazil, there is a reason Miller remains at the forefront.

"He was a member of the high-level class in Brazil," he said. "So, when he came back from the UK after his studies, he understood that he needed to bring the official association of football.

"When he came back to Brazil, he spread the modernity to the high-level society here."

While Miller's story may not be as well known in his adopted Hampshire home city today, Holley said Southampton FC has certainly not forgotten.

"Thankfully, the club are responsible for that mural on the wall and they've appreciated it for quite some time now that they've actually got a connection with football and Brazil from the early days."

title: MEN journo: Michael Carrick poised to have £66m man in his ranks for season-opener vs Hull City
description: Benjamin Sesko is poised to return to full fitness in time for Manchester United’s season-opener away to Hull City.The Red Devils kick off their 2026/2027 on Saturday, August 22 in the 12.30pm kick-...
fullText:
Benjamin Sesko is poised to return to full fitness in time for Manchester United's season-opener away to Hull City.

The Red Devils kick off their 2026/2027 on Saturday, August 22 in the 12.30pm kick-off and, according to Manchester Evening News' Steven Railston, the Slovenian is in line to make the squad.

Benjamin Sesko is still on track to be fit for the start of the season, so there's no reason to panic. The striker has been stepping up his rehabilitation at Carrington #mufc

Sesko has been ruled out of all of United's pre-season friendlies thus far due to a shin injury that was re-aggravated when he was barged off the pitch by Ibrahima Konate in last term's home win over Liverpool.

The 23-year-old was hooked at the interval and replaced by Amad Diallo. Little did he – or fans – know that Sesko would not feature again in the remaining three matches.

It meant he was unable to continue his scintillating run of form or add to his goal tally for his maiden campaign, so he ended 2025/2026 with 11 top-flight goals to his name in 30 appearances, which is still a hugely impressive feat for his first year in England.

Throughout the campaign, he was battling to secure a starting spot amid fierce competition from the likes of Amad, Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha.

He still managed to pop up with some crucial contributions, though, and returned seven goals in just 595 minutes played during Michael Carrick's reign.

His nation missing out on a World Cup spot did allow Sesko to spend the summer resting and not rushing to get fit or return prematurely, so there's no doubt he'll be chomping at the bit to get back out on the pitch in a competitive clash, having last featured on May 3.

Remarkably, reports this week have suggested that Bayern Munich have identified Sesko as their ideal long-term successor to world-class frontman Harry Kane.

title: A tale of two pitches as dry weather hits clubs
description: While Gainsborough Trinity are hoping for rain, Spalding United are enjoying a new artificial pitch.
fullText:
At one of the oldest football grounds in the country, staff are facing a very modern challenge ahead of the new season.

Non-league Gainsborough Trinity have played at the Northolme since 1884, but the stadium lacks the modern irrigation enjoyed by teams higher up the football pyramid.

It means their pitch has suffered from the heat and dry weather this summer.

Head groundsman John Wood says when he started at the Lincolnshire club three decades ago, "it was just a hose out of the changing room".

"Now, we have six in-pitch sprinklers and 17 around the edge which have been on constantly.

"We put around 20,000 litres of water on more or less every day."

Pitch renovations began at the Northolme – which has a claim to being the oldest ground in use continuously by a single team – in May.

But Wood says there has been very little rainfall since then and the Met Office recorded only 0.4mm (0.02in) in Lincolnshire in July.

The county is not officially in drought, but has experienced "prolonged dry weather", according to the government.

Anglian Water has imposed a hosepipe ban, but sports clubs can water pitches if they are actively being played on and would otherwise be dangerously hard.

With the water in short supply, Wood adds: "If this is going to be the norm, we are going to have to think of smarter ways to store water."

Sixty miles (97km) to the south, fellow non-league club Spalding United have managed to sidestep the problem.

In September last year, they completed a £1m upgrade to their stadium, the Sir Halley Stewart Playing Field, which included a "state-of-the-art" artificial pitch.

Promotion to the National League North followed and, for chief executive Leigh Porter, the prolonged dry weather has reinforced just why the investment was worthwhile.

"Having an artificial pitch has made this summer a lot more painless than what we would have had with a grass pitch," he says.

"We have really got a lovely facility, I wish I could wave a magic wand and give every club in the area the same pitch.

"I do not think there is a thing to call a game off because your pitch is too hard, but I think that is the danger."

Porter says the pitch can be used 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.

"It is right for our club and right for our community," he adds.

It is not just football clubs struggling with the dry weather.

On the coast in Skegness, the North Parade Bowling Greens CIC are due to host the English Bowls Federation finals at the end of August.

Steve O'Dare, the club's chairman, says preparations have been affected by the lack of rain.

"We have had to use our main irrigation system far more than we would like to because it is very expensive.

"We have no real idea of how much it is going to cost us but we have just got to bite the bullet and get some water on the greens."

He adds: "It is in the laps of whichever gods run this thing as to whether we get any water or not.

"If the bowling greens get dry, the surface is rougher and the bowls do not roll as they should do.

"It does not matter what forecast you look at, the rain is not coming. You have just got to keep fighting it."

title: Panic time for Dodgers? Losing streak hits 7 as Edwin Diaz blows save
description: The Dodgers' season-worst losing streak hit seven games after Edwin Diaz blew the save in Arizona.
fullText:
PHOENIX — The season was supposed to be over, right?

The World Series champion was crowned in August.

All that remained for the Los Angeles Dodgers was planning that World Series parade route.

Well, it has been a week since the Dodgers acquired two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal.

And they have yet to win a game.

They were walked off Friday night by the Arizona Diamondbacks, with Edwin Diaz blowing the save in their 4-3 loss.

And just like that, the Dodgers have lost seven consecutive games for the first time this season, outscored 46-25.

RYAN WALDSCHMIDT WALK-OFF HOMER! pic.twitter.com/awJyS4RYda

It took nearly a month before the Dodgers lost their seventh game of the season, and now, they have lost seven games in eight days, suffering two sweeps and now trying to avoid a third one.

Certainly, the Dodgers are in no real danger of blowing a 7½-game lead in the National League West over the Diamondbacks.

They are sitting comfortably in first place, and have absolutely no worries they'll win the division.

But suddenly, instead of having the best record in baseball, they have only the third-best in the NL, trailing Milwaukee and Atlanta.

If the season ended today, they'd be forced to play the wild-card round against the No. 6 seed, which would be the Philadelphia Phillies.

"A loss is a loss,'' Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said calmly, "but to get walked off never feels good. We didn't play a clean game, a great game on either side of the baseball, but we did enough to put ourselves in position to win the game.

"Unfortunately, we couldn't do it.''

It was Diaz, their $69 million closer, who blew the game.

He missed 85 games this year after undergoing arthroscopic elbow surgery in April, has come back and pitched four times, and hardly looks like the same All-Star pitcher. He has pitched three innings and given up six hits, four runs with four strikeouts and two walks.

And, yes, a blown save when he left a slider hanging over the plate to No. 9 hitter Ryan Waldschmidt, who smacked a 90-mph slider over the middle of the plate into the center-field seats.

"I'm just trying to be perfect with that pitch,'' Diaz said, "and I'm just missing right down the middle. I've got to be better than that. I'm a big-league pitcher, so I've got to make pitches. Next time when I come into the game, I've got to do better.''

Diaz, who signed a three-year, $69 million contract, the largest average salary for a reliever in baseball history, insists he feels healthy. He was still throwing his fastball 97 mph, and pretty much where he wanted. But it's that bread-and-butter pitch, the slider, that's betraying him.

"I think that everything what I've been doing is good,'' Diaz said, "but I don't know when I get into the game, I'm missing my (slider) right in the middle. … I've got a good fastball, but my slider, that's my strikeout pitch.

"I got to keep working. I'm still positive. I've just got to do my job better.''

The Dodgers are trying to stay positive, too, but know that if Diaz doesn't have his slider, he's only an ordinary reliever. And if he's only ordinary, the Dodgers have to find someone else who can close out games.

"I just think he just hasn't had the feel for that pitch,'' Roberts said, "since he got back. … I think it obviously sucks to go through it, but he's working hard to figure some things out. But it's one of those things that it's a little bit tougher when you're trying to work through it and you're at the back end of a game.

"It doesn't feel good, but I know the track record that he's working hard. He's not going to run from it. It's one of those things that you've got to kind of throw him into it, knowing he's healthy, and work himself out of it.''

The Dodgers are finding themselves in the same situation as a year ago. They acquired Diaz in the first place because Tanner Scott, who signed a four-year, $72 million contract the previous winter, couldn't handle the closer's role, blowing 10 saves. Now, they've got $141 million invested in closers and are still looking for the right guy.

When Roberts was asked if he would consider removing Diaz from the closer's role and using someone else, he was rather blunt.

"I think honestly,'' Roberts said, "you've got to look at the options, and see the way some of these guys are throwing. They're not throwing great, either. We've got to keep guys in their roles that they've earned, and try to get them on a run the way we were a few weeks ago.

"So, I just don't think there's a clear-cut alternative.''

The Dodgers wish that was their only problem these days. Their offense has been abysmal, too. They didn't produce their first hit off D-backs starter Merrill Kelly until Tommy Edman's infield single in the sixth inning. Their only extra-base hit was Andy Pages' go-ahead homer in the eighth inning. Their star quintet of Shohei Ohtani, Freddie Freeman, Max Muncy, Mookie Betts and Kyle Tucker went 2-for-16.

Tucker, who was supposed to be their solution in right field − they gave him a stagging four-year, $240 million contract − is hitting just .244 with 10 homers and a .719 OPS. He was summoned by Roberts into Roberts' office before the game just to make sure his confidence isn't eroding.

"I think he's in a good spot, I really do,'' Roberts said. "It hasn't been what anyone had hoped for up to this point, but for me, there's been some signs breaking. There's still a lot of baseball left, important baseball to play. But I think he's in a great headspace.''

Really, Roberts can say the same about his entire team. There's no panic. They've got Skubal now, who will make his first start at Dodger Stadium in a Dodger uniform on Monday. Fellow two-time Cy Young winner Blake Snell, who has pitched only three innings all season, is scheduled to start Tuesday. And Roki Sasaki turned in a strong outing Friday, giving up just four hits and two runs in six innings.

The Dodgers have endured rough stretches plenty of times through this dynasty. They lost seven games in a row last July. In 2017, the year they reached the World Series for the first time since 1988, they went through a 1-16 stretch. And still won 104 games.

"I remember,'' Roberts said. "It felt like we would never win another game. Well, we did win another game.

"And you know what? I know we'll win another game now, too.''

title: As Jackie the bald eagle fights for life, her doctors face harassment
description: Fans of the Big Bear Lake bald eagle have inundated a small raptor center with phone calls, online comments and even in-person visits. It's not helping.
fullText:
When a small raptor center in Southern California began caring for the most famous bald eagle on Earth, the keyboard veterinarians started piping up.

It started in mid-July when Jackie the bald eagle of Big Bear Lake arrived at the Ojai Raptor Center, about 170 miles from the home she shares with longtime partner Shadow. Jackie, who had fought off two other eagles in her territory but was suffering from a mysterious underlying illness, has now been at the facility for about three weeks and counting.

"Find the possible spider bite," suggested one woman on a health update about Jackie posted on July 23. Others were certain that Jackie's health would improve if the raptor center would only play her audio of Shadow and the couple's two eaglets. Another wondered if "the stress of being in confinement and away from her family will also make her give up."

As the posts flooded in, so did the phone calls. The raptor's small staff was quickly inundated to the point where they began pleading with people to let them concentrate on their work to help sick and injured birds. In recent days, the calls and social media posts have only snowballed.

"It's like a firehose of people having questions and emotions," said Jenny Voisard, a spokeswoman for Friends of Big Bear Valley, the group that made Jackie famous by installing the live 24/7 eagle nest camera that now streams in millions of homes across the world.

Complicating matters is the use of AI photos and misinformation on social media that have only stressed out Jackie's already anxious fan base. Some people have even accused the raptor center of only keeping Jackie to attract more donations, an upsetting allegation for the facility that takes in as many as 1,500 sick, injured or orphaned birds every year.

"Veterinarians, wildlife rehabilitators, and support staff increasingly face constant requests for information, repeated phone calls, unexpected visits, messages on their personal social media accounts, and, in some cases, contact at their private homes," the Ojai Raptor Center posted on Aug. 4. "While these actions are often driven by genuine concern, they can create significant distractions for the very people whose attention needs to remain on patient care."

As Jackie continues to fight for her life, USA TODAY is looking at some of the challenges facing her caregivers, why some of her fans are overwhelming them and the latest disheartening update about her health.

Jackie remains in critical condition in intensive care at the Ojai Raptor Center, where she's getting oxygen therapy, supportive treatment and around-the-clock monitoring, the facility shared in an update on Friday, Aug. 7.

It was the second time in recent days that Jackie's caregivers reported a decline in her packed cell volume, or the percentage of red blood cells in her stream. A normal range is between 35% and 55%. When Jackie first arrived to the facility, that figure was at 8% but had improved to 16% within a couple days. It's now back below 10%, the raptor center said Friday.

"We know how deeply many of you care about this eagle, and we understand how difficult it is to receive an update like this," center Director Chris Eksteen said in a video update. "We wish we had better news to share."

Jackie's caregivers are consulting closely with specialists across the country as they "determine the next steps in her care."

Eksteen said that a CT scan and bone marrow biopsy that Jackie underwent this week "have provided our veterinary team with important new information, but we do not yet have the complete picture." He said the team is conducting some additional specialized testing.

"At this stage, our priority is to provide (Jackie) with the supportive care that she needs, while closely monitoring her welfare and allowing our veterinary team and consulting specialists the time necessary to carefully evaluate this week's findings," he said. "Every decision that we make continues to be guided by her medical condition, her welfare, and what is in her best interest."

Update on Jackie: Beloved bald eagle critical as blood levels drop again

In the roughly three weeks since Jackie has been at the Ojai Raptor Center, her caregivers have provided nine health updates, along with many photos and videos of her care. One video they shared showed Jackie being hand-fed, sitting in an oxygen chamber, being placed under anesthesia for diagnostic testing, and getting a blood transfusion that initially saved her life.

When several days go by without an update, her fans get anxious and some of them get angry. Someone even began an online petition demanding more updates.

"Heartbreak has turned to frustration. Fans and wildlife advocates are struggling to get clear, consistent information about Jackie's condition and care," the petition says. "The agencies and organizations responsible for her care have a responsibility to keep the public informed − not just with vague status updates, but with meaningful transparency about her diagnosis, treatment plan, and prognosis . . . The millions who love her deserve to know."

The raptor center has said they are sharing new information when they have it. The Friends of Big Bear Valley has denounced the petition, saying this week that it "does nothing for Jackie, hinders her care team and only heightens people's anxiety over the situation."

"It is important to let Ojai do their job without interruptions. Please do not call, text, show up at their doors, or demand frequent updates," the group posted on Facebook.

"It is a disappointment to see individuals leaving nasty comments on Ojai Raptor Centers Facebook updates and elsewhere," the group continued. "Their goal is to get Jackie healthy and release her back to her territory, please let them do their job."Voisard believes that people are overwhelming the raptor center, and Friends of Big Bear Valley, because they are preparing themselves for the worst and even pre-grieving the beloved bald eagle, triggering a stress response in some of them.

"It's really freaking people out and what people tend to do in this situation, because there's a lack of control and visibility, and certainty, they try to seek out information as a way of coping," she said. "We're experiencing that on steroids because of social media and because of Jackie's fanbase."

In a post this week about the dangers of social media and AI, the Ojai Raptor Center said that "stories can travel around the world in minutes."

"Artificial intelligence can generate convincing photographs, videos, and articles that appear authentic but are entirely fabricated," the center wrote. "Rumors quickly become accepted as fact, and speculation is often repeated long before accurate information is available. For the people caring for wildlife, this comes at a cost."

Wildlife medicine "requires concentration, careful decision making, and often long hours of uninterrupted work," the center said. "Every unnecessary interruption takes time and focus away from the animals depending on us."

With Friday's latest bad news about Jackie, Friends of Big Bear Valley shared some positive coping mechanisms for her stressed-out fans.

They can do something as simple as praying and thinking positive thoughts or something more active, like learning about their local wildlife rescue organizations and finding out how they can help, from volunteering to donating.

People can also research where in their area they would take an ill or injured animal and save that information for if and when the time comes.

Voisard recommends that people take a break from social media, avoid wading into the comments and if it's too distressing, not to watch the videos showing Jackie's treatment.

"The best thing is to stay positive," she said. "Don't pre-grieve until it's time, don't put that on yourself. We're not there yet. Choose to be positive until you know otherwise because it doesn't do her or us any good."

Whatever happens to Queen Jackie, as her biggest fans fondly call her, the Ojai Raptor Center said in one recent post that she has "changed the future" and inspired millions of people to donate their money to protect habitat near her nest.

"The result is far bigger than one nest or one eagle," the center said. "Generations of Bald Eagles, and all the wildlife that depends on this landscape can continue to thrive. That is the true power of conservation."

Amanda Lee Myers is a senior crime reporter who covers the death penalty, cold case investigations, breaking news − and sometimes eagles − for USA TODAY. Follow her on X at @amandaleeusat.

title: Iran’s leaders believe a victory is within reach, and that time is on their side
description: The Strait of Hormuz is, by some accounts, named for a Zoroastrian deity destined to emerge victorious after a 9,000-year standoff with an adversary.  Iran's leaders feel their own victory is at hand ...
fullText:
The Strait of Hormuz is, by some accounts, named for a Zoroastrian deity destined to emerge victorious after a 9,000-year standoff with an adversary.

Iran's leaders feel their own victory is at hand and won't require the same epic patience.

They are betting that military pressure will ultimately force the United States to accept their control over the crucial waterway for global energy — and that time is on their side.

They know about the diminishing stockpiles of key U.S. weapons such as advanced missile interceptors. They know the war is deeply unpopular with Americans. They know that as long as the strait is largely closed, the price of gas and other goods will stay high ahead of U.S. congressional elections in November. They know that trying to open it by force would be costly and may require American ground troops. They know their Houthi allies in Yemen could widen the war and disrupt another major trade route.

But Iran's strategy carries risks.

Trump points to strikes that have decimated Iran's top leadership, navy and air force. He alternates between threatening escalation and saying talks are going well. Iran's own economy has been battered, in part because of a U.S. blockade. Iranians rose up in mass protests just months ago and could do so again.

And Iran's leaders need only look to how Trump's "short-term excursion" to the Middle East has bogged down to be reminded that wars rarely turn out as expected.

Iran says it is close to reaching a deal with Oman to manage the strait, which runs between the two countries. But it would be conditioned on the U.S. lifting its blockade, so even if there are no direct negotiations — as Iran says — Trump would have to approve.

It's unclear whether the deal would allow Iran to charge fees. But it would formalize its control over what had been an open international waterway before the war, one that carried a fifth of the world's traded oil and gas.

Abdolreza Davari, an analyst who once advised former President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, said Iran's effective control of the strait has given it leverage with the U.S. and regional countries that can help guarantee its security.

"More than revenue from the strait, Iran wants to confirm its management and sovereignty over the strait," he said by phone from Tehran.

Formal control over even part of the strait would be a clear win for Iran and a loss for the U.S., which has yet to accomplish some of its various and shifting goals in the war.

It would also deal a blow to global norms on freedom of navigation and set a precedent that much of the world would find disturbing — that nations can shut down trade choke points at will.

China, which buys oil from Iran and has influence over it, said as recently as May that "normal and safe passage" through the strait should be restored.

To borrow a phrase from Trump's own theory of geopolitics, Iran believes it holds the cards.

"They started the war, but its end was never with them. We always decide for ourselves when it ends," Mahdi Mohammadi, an adviser to Iran's chief negotiator, posted on social media. "Iran is going after the enemy's defeat — not an agreement."

He said a surprise Iranian attack on Jordan in July "compensated" for a drop in oil prices. That contributed to the collapse of an interim agreement reached in June that had offered significant concessions to Iran, including a U.S. waiver to sell oil internationally and the promise of broader sanctions relief.

Iran has repeatedly said the Strait of Hormuz will not go back to being an open waterway, and that it will keep attacking ships trying to transit without its permission. Iran's joint military command has called it an "unbreakable red line."

"For Iran, the Strait of Hormuz has become a strategic lever for deterrence, maintaining the regional balance of power, and reshaping the security rules in the Persian Gulf," said Mostafa Najafi, a Tehran-based security analyst.

That poses a major obstacle to ending the war, much less resolving the even more complex, long-standing dispute over Iran's nuclear program.

"The atomic issue, because of the conflict in the Strait of Hormuz, has been pushed to the side, and in reality, that is in Iran's interests," said Rahman Ghahremanpour, an Iran-based analyst. Control of the strait would give Iran leverage if the nuclear talks resume, he added.

The economic fallout from the war has spread worldwide but is particularly acute in Iran.

U.S. and Israeli strikes have pummeled its industrial base. The U.S. blockade has choked off much of its oil exports. Iranians are grappling with triple-digit food inflation. Trump has repeatedly threatened major strikes on civilian infrastructure like water and electricity.

In December, a currency crisis sparked some of the biggest anti-government protests in the 47-year history of the Islamic Republic. Authorities responded with a bloody crackdown in which thousands were killed and tens of thousands detained.

Many in Iran, including those close to its moderate President Masoud Pezeshkian, fear it may go too far.

Mohammad Javad Zarif, who as foreign minister helped negotiate the 2015 nuclear deal, wrote in a recent essay that Iran's achievements in the war had opened "an exceptional window for diplomacy." But he warned that if it doesn't strike a deal soon, then "economic recovery will be difficult, and the possibility of internal unrest or renewed aggression, especially after the U.S. elections, cannot be ruled out."

The war has already been marked by surprises.

After the first wave of U.S. and Israeli airstrikes on Feb. 28 killed Iran's supreme leader and other top officials, Trump suggested it would be over in a matter of weeks.

Instead, the conflict has emboldened Iran's leaders and mobilized their supporters. Tehran is using the strait "to show that it has not been defeated," Ghahremanpour said. "It can increase its legitimacy at home."

But the strategy could also backfire. Iran's resilience has limits and there are concerns that an economic crash could trigger unrest. "Iran cannot continue with this strategy forever, and at a certain point, in reality, it has to reach a deal with America," he said.

But Davari said that for now, Iran can withstand the pressure. "It's unlikely, despite the difficulties of the economic situation, that Iran will retreat from its positions," he said.

Krauss has reported from across the Middle East for more than 20 years, including postings in Cairo, Baghdad and Jerusalem. Radjy is a Cairo-based journalist who has reported on Iran for over a decade.

title: US intel assesses Putin could launch attack aimed at testing NATO unity
description: Recent US intelligence assessments indicate Russian President Vladimir Putin could try to test NATO’s resolve by launching a limited attack on an allied country within the next few years, according to...
fullText:
Recent US intelligence assessments indicate Russian President Vladimir Putin could try to test NATO's resolve by launching a limited attack on an allied country within the next few years, according to three sources familiar with those reports.

The intelligence assessments outline several possible scenarios for Russian escalation, ranging from a cyberattack to a small-scale incursion intended to challenge NATO's unity and commitment to Article 5, which states that an attack on one member is an attack on all, without necessarily crossing the threshold for an allied response, the sources said.

While how and when Putin might do so remains an open question, one of the sources said he is most likely to escalate in some way by targeting the Baltics or Poland. The Wall Street Journal first reported on the recent assessments.

US and NATO officials believe Putin may choose to escalate against NATO if he is unable to secure a face-saving off-ramp to the war with Ukraine, the sources added, noting the Russian president's window for choosing his next course of action spans between now and the next few years.

Martin O'Donnell, a senior NATO military spokesperson, declined to comment on classified intelligence assessments but said NATO is "always thinking through and preparing for any number of scenarios."

"NATO is watching and we are ready to deter and defend as necessary, which we continue to demonstrate," he added.

There have been numerous instances over the last few years of Russia encroaching on NATO territory. In May, a drone carrying explosives hit an apartment building in Romania as Russian forces attacked a nearby Ukrainian port, injuring two people. And last September, NATO fighter jets shot down multiple Russian drones that had violated Polish airspace during an attack on Ukraine.

And just this week, the US assessed that an explosive-laden drone discovered at an airport in Germany overnight on Wednesday belonged to a Russian intelligence service, a US defense official in Europe told CNN. The official said the drone was carrying military-grade explosives; CNN previously reported it was discovered by an airport staff member in a secure area of cargo flight operations.

CNN asked the Kremlin for comment on the US intel assessment on Putin as well as the assessment on the drone.

"Drone sightings, drone threats including in a hybrid context, are something we know from the past," German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt told reporters on Wednesday. "That a drone armed with explosives is at an airport is a new threat scenario."

Dobrindt indicated Thursday that the drone could be tied to "foreign powers" though he stopped short of providing specifics.

The German National Security Council, led by Chancellor Friedrich Merz, met on Friday to discuss the airport incident.

The intelligence assessments on Russia's plans also come amid heightened concerns over the US' munitions stockpile which has been significantly depleted in the war against Iran, and an increase in civilian casualties from Russian long-range weapons.

CNN previously reported that nearly 80% of its THAAD missile interceptors — a key missile defense system — have been exhausted in the war compared to pre-war levels, as well as roughly half of its Patriot interceptors. Meanwhile, the UN has said that civilian casualties from Russian long-range weapons increased 60% between January to June, compared to the same period last year.

In one night of attacks this week, Russian ballistic and anti-ship missiles killed at least 17 people and wounded dozens more. None of the missiles were intercepted by Ukrainian defenses, CNN reported.

Concerns over key munitions and interceptors are impacting the way senior military commanders are planning for potential future conflict, including escalation against NATO by Putin or war with China in the Pacific.

President Donald Trump has privately complained in recent days about reports of the US' dwindling stockpiles due to the war with Iran, including last week at a Cabinet meeting at Camp David, six sources familiar with the meeting previously told CNN.

"The U.S. has massive amounts of 'munitions,' especially of certain types," Trump said on Truth Social late Thursday night. "Additionally, large amounts are being manufactured and shipped to the U.S. as needed. Defense companies are building the largest number of plants and factories in our country's history."

The recent intelligence assessments also come as US-led diplomatic efforts to bring the war between Russia and Ukraine to an end have stalled. Ongoing US and European sanctions against Moscow have had an impact on Russia's economy but have not stopped Putin's continued assault on Ukraine.

title: Memphis forward Brandon Clarke died from effects of heroin and cocaine, authorities say
description: Memphis Grizzlies forward Brandon Clarke died in May from the effects of heroin and cocaine, authorities said Friday.  The Los Angeles County Department of Medical Examiner said the 29-year-old basketball player's death was accidental.  Clarke was found dead inside a home near Los Angeles on May 11.
fullText:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Memphis Grizzlies forward Brandon Clarke died in May from the effects of heroin and cocaine, authorities said Friday.

The Los Angeles County Department of Medical Examiner said the 29-year-old basketball player's death was accidental.

Clarke was found dead inside a home near Los Angeles on May 11. A person familiar with the terms of the investigation told The Associated Press after the Grizzlies announced Clarke's passing that drug paraphernalia was found at the residence. The person had spoken on condition of anonymity because those details had not been released publicly.

Clarke was under contract to be with the Grizzlies through the 2026-27 season.

About six weeks before he died, Clarke was arrested in Arkansas on charges of speeding, reckless driving and possessing a controlled substance. He was with Memphis for all seven of his pro seasons after finishing his college career at Gonzaga.
